body.statement: For every \(n\ge4\), the explicit model \(\mathfrak F_n\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_{\mathsf A}(1/40,1/2,32)\). Every fixed-coordinate covariance has spectrum in \([1/32,32]\); the transcript \(\mathfrak T_{\mathsf A}(P)\) has exactly \(n^2+2n-2\) matrix occurrences; every reached positive eigenvalue is at least \(1/40\); every reached graph comparison is zero or one; and both the printed source scale and the valid reciprocal scale satisfy \(\gamma^{\ast}(G)=\rho^{\ast}(G)=1\). The source thresholds obey \(\gamma_{\mathrm{src}}=1/4\in(0,\gamma^{\ast}(G))\), whereas its rank-threshold premise fails because \(\eta_{\mathrm{src}}=1/80\) and the subset \(\{3,4\}\) is not reached but \[\eta^{\ast}(P)\le\lambda_{\min}^{+}(R(\{3,4\}))\le2^{-2n-1}<1/80.\] The family also satisfies every non-margin condition of Acartürk et al.'s graph theorem: the induced support-coordinate densities and causal conditionals are strictly positive and continuously differentiable, there is one distinct single-target intervention per node, their Assumption 1 parent-ratio condition holds, and the empirical Gaussian covariance score-difference estimator satisfies their consistency condition (15).
body.justification: The family is simultaneously a constant reached-gap Gaussian fixture and a legal published-class witness against necessity of equation \(22\).
body.gap: The source's sufficient analysis gives no all-dimension legal family separating executed spectral geometry from an exponentially small unused subset margin.
body.consumer: It tests that warnings and precision depend on reached operations rather than the unqueried subset \(\{3,4\}\).
body.proof_tex:
Put \(\epsilon=2^{-n}\).  The structural matrix of \(\mathfrak F_n\) has nonzero rows only at labels \(3\) and \(4\), with parent vectors \(b_3=(1,1)\) and \(b_4=(1,1+\epsilon)\).  Thus \(B^2=0\) and \(\|B\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\|B\|_{\mathrm F}<3\); deleting any one target row preserves these properties.  Since \((I-B^{(m)})^{-1}=I+B^{(m)}\) and each intervention-noise covariance has spectrum in \([1,2]\),
\[
 \lambda_{\max}(\Sigma_m)
 \le2\|I+B^{(m)}\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2<32,
 \qquad
 \lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_m)
 \ge\|(I+B^{(m)})^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}^{-2}>1/16.
 \tag{20}
\]
Hence every fixed-coordinate covariance has spectrum in \([1/32,32]\).  The construction directly verifies the linear Gaussian DAG equations, graph compatibility, perfect single-target variance resets, and full-rank mixing with \(G=I_n\); independent streams can be sampled in all environments.

For a reset root,
\[
 R_i=\frac14e_ie_i^{\top}.
 \tag{21}
\]
For a child with parent vector \(b\), write \(s=b^{\top}(Z_1,Z_2)\) and \(E=Z_c-s\).  Under the observational law, \(s\) and \(E\) are independent and the score difference is \(d_c=(-bE,(E-s)/2)\).  Therefore, on the parent plane and coordinate \(c\),
\[
 R_c=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 bb^{\top}&-b/2\\
 -b^{\top}/2&(1+\|b\|_2^2)/4
 \end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{col}(R_c)=\operatorname{span}\{b,e_c\}.
 \tag{22}
\]
In the orthonormal basis \(b/\|b\|_2,e_c\), put \(B_0=\|b\|_2^2\in[2,5]\).  The nonzero block has determinant \(B_0^2/4\) and trace \((5B_0+1)/4\), so
\[
 \lambda_{\min}^{+}(R_c)
 \ge\frac{B_0^2}{5B_0+1}\ge\frac4{11},
 \qquad
 R_c\succeq\frac4{11}P_{\operatorname{span}\{b,e_c\}}.
 \tag{23}
\]

Every nonempty subset of the four core labels other than \(\{3,4\}\) has positive eigenvalues at least \(1/40\).  Root-only sets have gap \(1/4\), and child singletons have gap at least \(4/11\).  If a set contains one root \(i\) and a child with parent vector \(b\), then
\[
 \lambda_{\min}^{+}(P_{e_i}+P_b)
 =1-|e_i^{\top}b|/\|b\|_2
 \ge1-2/\sqrt5>1/10.
\]
Multiplying by \(\min\{1/4,4/11\}=1/4\) gives a parent-plane lower bound greater than \(1/40\), while (23) supplies the child coordinate with coefficient \(4/11\).  Adding the other child preserves that bound and supplies its orthogonal child coordinate; adding the other root gives the direct parent-plane bound \((1/4)I_2\).  These cases exhaust the core subsets other than \(\{3,4\}\).  Every label at least \(5\) contributes an orthogonal eigenvalue \(1/4\).

The population leaf-removal order is
\[
 (3,4,1,2,5,6,\ldots,n),
\]
so the reversed topological order is \(\pi=(n,n-1,\ldots,5,2,1,4,3)\).  In the first order round, deleting one label retains a core root whenever both children remain; after label \(3\) is removed, no later order query contains both children.  In any graph query containing both children, both core roots already lie in the prefix, descendant deletion removes no root, and deletion of the current row removes at most one root.  Singleton encoder queries contain only one child.  Thus no reached occurrence has core intersection exactly \(\{3,4\}\).  The preceding subset bounds prove that every reached positive eigenvalue is at least \(1/40\).

For every graph query, descendant pruning leaves an ancestral set.  Removing the current label deletes its coordinate exactly when it is a leaf; otherwise (22) lets a remaining child's parent vector supply the coordinate.  Both ranges are consequently coordinate subspaces, so their projector-product norm is zero or one.  This proves the reached projector band with \(h_0=1/2\), using actual projectors rather than the source's printed angular expression.

The order phase evaluates \(\sum_{t=2}^nt=n(n+1)/2-1\) matrix occurrences.  The graph phase contributes \(n-1\) prefix occurrences and \(n(n-1)/2\) comparison-sum occurrences, and the encoder phase contributes \(n\) singletons.  Hence the total is
\[
 n(n+1)/2-1+(n-1)+n(n-1)/2+n=n^2+2n-2.
 \tag{24}
\]

For the unqueried subset, the four vectors \(e_3,b_3,e_4,b_4\) are independent because \(\det(b_3,b_4)=\epsilon\ne0\).  Thus \(R(\{3,4\})\) is positive definite on the four-dimensional core.  With \(v=(1,-1,0,0)^{\top}/\sqrt2\), (22) gives
\[
 v^{\top}R_3v=0,
 \qquad
 v^{\top}R_4v=\epsilon^2/2.
\]
The Rayleigh variational principle yields
\[
 \eta^{\ast}(P)
 \le\lambda_{\min}^{+}(R(\{3,4\}))
 \le\epsilon^2/2=2^{-2n-1}<1/80.
 \tag{25}
\]
Since \(G=H=I_n\), \(\gamma^{\ast}(G)=\rho^{\ast}(G)=1\), while \(\eta_{\mathrm{src}}=1/80\) and \(\gamma_{\mathrm{src}}=1/4\).

Finally, every Gaussian density and every causal conditional is strictly positive and continuously differentiable.  Let \(\phi_v\) denote the centered Gaussian density of variance \(v\).  A root intervention has a nonconstant ratio of centered Gaussian densities.  For a child, differentiating
\[
 \frac{\phi_2(z_c)}{\phi_1(z_c-b^{\top}z_{\mathrm{pa}(c)})}
\]
in either parent coordinate gives a nonzero function because both parent coefficients are nonzero.  Hence the source's Assumption 1 parent-ratio condition holds, and a perfect stochastic intervention is a legal special case of its smooth soft-intervention model.  Entrywise laws of large numbers give \(S_{m,r}\to\Sigma_m\) in probability.  On the uniformly positive-definite neighborhood,
\[
 S_{m,r}^{-1}-\Sigma_m^{-1}
 =S_{m,r}^{-1}(\Sigma_m-S_{m,r})\Sigma_m^{-1}
\]
gives inverse convergence, and multiplication by a Gaussian vector of finite second moment gives the source's squared-mean score-difference consistency.  Thus all promised-class assumptions and all stated non-margin source conditions hold.  Equations (20), (24), and (25) establish every remaining assertion.
